naive.meaning: marked by or showing unaffected simplicity and lack of guile or worldly experience
naive.example: a teenager's naive ignorance of life

nanny.meaning: a woman who is the custodian of children

nasal.meaning: of or in or relating to the nose

naval.meaning: connected with or belonging to or used in a navy

navel.meaning: a scar where the umbilical cord was attached
navel.example: you were not supposed to show your navel on television

needy.meaning: needing a lot of attention; poor

nerve.meaning: a fibre that carries signals in the body; courage

never.example: I have never been to China

niche.meaning: a position particularly well suited to the person who occupies it
niche.example: he found his niche in the academic world

niece.meaning: a daughter of your brother or sister

night.meaning: the time after sunset and before sunrise while it is dark outside

ninth.meaning: coming next after the eighth and just before the tenth in position

noble.meaning: having high moral qualities; of aristocratic rank

noise.meaning: sound of any kind (especially unintelligible or dissonant sound)

noisy.meaning: full of or characterized by loud and nonmusical sounds

nomad.meaning: a member of a people who have no permanent home but move about according to the seasons

noose.meaning: a loop of rope that tightens when pulled

north.meaning: the direction to your left when facing the sunrise

notch.meaning: a small V-shaped cut; a level

novel.meaning: an extended fictional work in prose

nudge.example: She nudged my elbow when she saw her friend enter the restaurant

nurse.meaning: one skilled in caring for young children or the sick (usually under the supervision of a physician)

nylon.meaning: a strong synthetic fabric or fibre

nymph.meaning: (classical mythology) a minor nature goddess usually depicted as a beautiful maiden
nymph.example: the ancient Greeks believed that nymphs inhabited forests and bodies of water
